audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Skill, Jayce, Jayce, Skill, Skill, Jayce, Jayce while whys[0] says he chunks you for free at Level 1, whys[2] calls Level 3 'your first even window', whys[3] gives him the poke advantage through 4-5 and whys[5] calls first item 'roughly even'.
audit.why: The mirror audit (jayce vs graves) is already on disk and set the chart to Jayce, Jayce, Skill, Jayce, Skill, Skill, Jayce. Both directions must state the same stages.
audit.corrected: Chart flipped as one atomic group to Jayce, Jayce, Skill, Jayce, Skill, Skill, Jayce, with the four affected phase whys rewritten and the Level 1 rating dropped to 4/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as a clean Graves spike. The mirror already corrected this on his side: 6 is contested, and his spikes are Acceleration Gate at 2-3 and his first item.
audit.why: Collateral Damage (100s at rank 1, 1000 range) buys you one punish per fight, not a level you own; his Shock Blast poke pattern is unchanged by it.
audit.corrected: Level 6 kept as the even kill window with the real range and cooldown, and Thundering Blow's 20s rank-1 timer written into the 4-5 phase as the thing that actually decides your commits.

audit.whatIsWrong: Collateral Damage is called 'a wall escape' / 'a wall-dash escape' in whys[4], spikes[2] and mid. Riot's R text is damage to the first champion then a cone explosion — there is no self-displacement. report[10] also repeats the false Smoke Screen blind.
audit.why: A player holding R as an escape button will die holding it. Quickdraw is the only exit in this kit.
audit.corrected: R restated as a 1000-range nuke with Quickdraw named as the exit. Smoke Screen restated as sight cut plus slow, matching the mirror's nearsight wording already used in whys[2] and wants.you[2].

edits.before: Four shells of buckshot win any level-1 face-off — trade autos point-blank where every pellet lands.
edits.after: Gate-accelerated Shock Blast outranges your whole kit and you hold no Quickdraw to close — free chunks.

edits.before: Full kit: Q's wall-bounce return is your real damage — fight near terrain so both hits connect.
edits.after: Q, W and E together: dash in, fog him, and trade point-blank — your first even window.

edits.before: Trade in shell rhythm: two autos and out. Track Shock Blast; your armor stacks from E make his short trades unprofitable.
edits.after: True Grit wins extended melee, but Thundering Blow (20s at rank 1) knocks you back out every time you commit.

edits.before: First item spike — the point-blank Q-AA-E-AA pattern now removes half bars. Force fights near walls.
edits.after: First item is even — Eclipse lets you gap-close and shred, but his cannon poke matches it at range.

edits.before: Collateral Damage gives you a burst nuke and a wall escape, so you can finally punish a Jayce who walks up to poke — even kill window.
edits.after: Collateral Damage gives you a 1000-range burst nuke, so you can finally punish a Jayce who steps up to poke — an even kill window.

edits.before: Collateral Damage gives you a real burst nuke plus a wall-dash escape — your best window to punish a Jayce who stepped up to land cannon poke.
edits.after: Collateral Damage gives you a real 1000-range burst nuke — your best window to punish a Jayce who stepped up to land cannon poke, with a Quickdraw charge held for the exit.

edits.before: Through 4-5 your True Grit stacks and your second Quickdraw charge make you tankier in any sustained melee exchange, but the problem is reaching melee at all — every time you Quickdraw in, his hammer-stance Thundering Blow knocks you straight back out and he flips to cannon to poke the difference. At 6 your R is your equalizer: Collateral Damage is a huge nuke and a wall-dash escape, so when he steps up to land cannon poke, Quickdraw in, Smoke Screen to nearsight him, and R him for the kill. That's your single best kill window. The honest read: if he plays at range and only commits when you're already low on his poke, you never get a clean all-in, and you bleed out of lane down CS and HP.
edits.after: Through 4-5 your True Grit stacks and your second Quickdraw charge make you tankier in any sustained melee exchange, but the problem is reaching melee at all — every time you Quickdraw in, his hammer-stance Thundering Blow (20s at rank 1) knocks you straight back out and he flips to cannon to poke the difference. At 6 your R is the equalizer: Collateral Damage is a huge 1000-range nuke, so when he steps up to land cannon poke, Quickdraw in, Smoke Screen to nearsight him, and R him for the kill — keep the second dash, because the R is not an escape. The honest read: if he only commits once his poke has you low, you never get a clean all-in and you bleed out of lane.

edits.before: Your W smoke blinds tower dives and breaks gank pathing — drop it on arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.
edits.after: Smoke Screen cuts sight and slows on impact — no blind. Drop it as the gank arrives and fight them blind-sided in the fog.

notes: Chart restated to match the already-written mirror (jayce__graves): Jayce, Jayce, Skill, Jayce, Skill, Skill, Jayce. Removed the fabricated 'wall escape / wall-dash escape' attached to Collateral Damage in three places — Riot's R text has no self-displacement, and Quickdraw is the only exit. Smoke Screen blind claim removed from report[10]; the nearsight wording the mirror introduced was already correct in whys[2] and wants.you[2].
